classification.difficultyReason: Find two ground distances using tangent, then combine them using Pythagoras' theorem.

spec.description: Vertical pole with two sight lines, two ground legs, a joining ground segment and elevation angles. The foot marker explicitly belongs to the two ground legs. Decorative power lines and pole hardware are omitted; ordinary geometry is black.
spec.mathematics: Pole height 10 m; elevations 45 degrees and 30 degrees; perpendicular ground legs; joining ground distance x.

answer.worked:
Let $a$ and $b$ be the two ground distances from the foot of the pole.
$$\begin{aligned}a&=\frac{10}{\tan45^\circ}=10\text{ m}\\b&=\frac{10}{\tan30^\circ}=10\sqrt3\text{ m}\\x^2&=a^2+b^2\\x&=\sqrt{10^2+(10\sqrt3)^2}\\x&=20\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
